presentation.notes_en: Meanings of the solo and stilt passage come from the creators’ published accounts. The circle is not translated into a claim about real-life experiences, and the work’s LGBTQ subject does not establish any participant’s sexual orientation. The apple sequence is reported by the performance article; the four time points describe stills. Names follow published text, not facial identification. Original “Photos for” labels are not photographer credits. The complete source file matches the approved upload receipt by SHA-256; times belong only to this 44:26 edit and player seek precision depends on the platform. Exact boundaries of the solo and stilt passage and the second-floor seating arrangement are not established. This update did not involve continuous listening or viewing.
presentation.notes_zh: 独舞和高跷的含义来自创作者公开自述；“圈”不转换为现实遭遇，作品的LGBTQ议题不用于推断参与者性取向。苹果动作经过来自演后报道，四个时间点对应静帧观察；人物姓名沿用原文，不由面孔辨认。原始照片标签Photos for不作摄影署名。成片完整源文件与既有上传回执SHA-256一致，时间只适用于这支44:26剪辑版；播放器定位精度以平台为准。尚未登记独舞、高跷段落精确起止，未确认二楼座位安排；本轮没有连续听看影片。

## 从一个招募问题进入《茧房》
《茧房》的公开材料留下了几种不同的相遇方式：招募文案邀请人走进排练，宣传稿把制作叙述成一段共同投入的时间，预告邀请观众接近作品，44分26秒剪辑版则让舞台上的身体和空间可以反复观看。把它们放在一起，首先能读到的是一次创作怎样被邀请、讲述和保存；从邀请到实际排练的每一步，仍需相应过程记录。
招募稿提出招收5至8名舞者，年龄不限，也不要求专业舞蹈基础。这是公开写出的进入条件，不能由此推断成片中谁具有或不具有专业训练。[S1] 下面的阅读沿着文稿中的制作时间，进入同一成片的三个观察点，再回到尚待核实的排练问题。

## 文稿给出时间线，也留下一个需要对照的差异
《在p4剧场的16个日与夜的期盼》把制作写成连续的推进：9月敲定排期，10月初完成招募，10月16日开始排练，面向10月31日公演。它还列举演员、舞者、灯光、记录、导演、主持、宣传、编导、观众、道具和制作等环节，显示这篇宣传文字如何把演出呈现为多种工作的汇合。[S2]
另一份整合宣传草稿却写演员在10月15日才定下来，排练时间约半个月，并列出10月31日19:30的演出安排。[S3] “完成招募”和“演员定下来”可能指不同环节，也可能来自不同稿本的叙述。这里保留两种措辞，不选一个日期冒充已经核实的排练史。这是可以继续追查的具体线索：招募收束、人员确认和开始排练之间，究竟怎样衔接？
这些日期目前是历史宣传文稿中的说法。文件保存顺序不足以确定稿本先后，宣传中的时间安排也不能替代出勤表或逐日排练记录。

## 邀请并未止于入组：文稿还把观众带向演出之后
另一份宣传草稿提出正式演出后的身体即兴体验：由演员带领观众以身体沟通，重新感知周围空间，继续参与舞台创作。[S4] 与演员招募稿并读，可以看见两层进入方式：先招募参与制作的人，再邀请观看者参与演出后的活动。[S1][S4]
这是文稿层面明确的工作构想。它使我们能提出更具体的问题：带领怎样开始，观众如何进入演区，表演与体验的边界怎样交接？目前这几份文稿和下列成片静帧都不足以证明当晚按计划执行了这项活动，也不能把成片中的群体画面直接标作观众体验。

## 从同一成片的三个位置观察身体与空间
先打开44分26秒舞台作品剪辑版，再用三个已核静帧回到影片。它们取自该公开版的同一上传文件，时间只属于这一个版本。[V1]
18:00：红色光线勾勒出表演者的跨步姿态，腿部外侧可见装置。可观察的是身体轮廓、跨步与光的关系；装置本身不提供身体状况或人物身份的依据。[V3]
33:00：同一画面中出现站立、蹲坐和侧卧的身体，演区因此呈现不同高度。由此可以追问空间如何由多个位置共同构成。单帧没有保存位置形成的过程，应返回连续影片查看前后变化。[V4]
38:00：前景的伸臂与后景较低的人群形成前后层次，不同手臂方向提供另一种空间对照。[V5] 这三个观察点给观众一条可操作的观看路径：从一个身体与光的关系，转向多个身体的高度，再看前后景及方向。它是本次编辑安排的阅读顺序，不是对排练阶段、角色或编舞意图的断言。

## 预告、成片和文稿各自保留什么
1分16秒数字版预告承担宣传入口的作用；44分26秒剪辑版提供较长的舞台观看入口。两者分别保存，预告时码不能换算为成片时码。[V2][V1] 成片页还保留既有主频道版本，方便核对访问版本；没有经验证的跨版本时间对应时，应从各自入口阅读。
文稿记录进入条件、制作叙述和预期活动；成片静帧记录这一剪辑版本在特定时刻可见的姿态与空间。两种证据可以帮助提出同一个项目的问题，却不能彼此代替：开放招募是否带来了不同的工作方法，需要排练过程支持；舞台上可见的群体关系，也不能直接证明制作中的共识。

## 下一步怎样把线索变成过程叙述
最优先的两项核对已经具体化。第一，对照招募收束与演员确认的不同表述，寻找能标明日期和修订的排练安排。第二，对照演后身体即兴的计划，寻找独立记录来区分“提出活动”和“实际带领”。[S2][S3][S4]
下方来源可以逐条核对，观看引用可返回成片与预告，侧栏连接《茧房》项目和“邀请怎样进入排练”问题档案。这一页先让公开文稿与可见画面形成可追踪的阅读关系；后续获得新的公开证据时，再修订具体过程判断并保留本版。
saved_article_versions.body_en:
## Entering Cocoon through an invitation
The public materials for Cocoon offer several ways into the work. A recruitment notice invites people into rehearsal; publicity describes production as a period of shared commitment; a trailer introduces the work; and a 44:26 edited stage film makes bodies and stage space available for repeated viewing. Read together, they show how a production was invited, narrated and preserved. Establishing what happened at each step still requires process evidence.
The recruitment text seeks five to eight dancers, sets no age limit and does not require professional dance training. These are stated entry conditions, not evidence of the training of any person visible in the film.[S1] This reading follows the production timeline described in the documents, moves through three moments in one film edition, and returns to specific rehearsal questions.

## A production timeline with an unresolved difference
The text titled Sixteen Days and Nights of Anticipation at P4 presents a sequence: scheduling in September, recruitment completed in early October, rehearsals beginning on 16 October, and a public performance planned for 31 October. It lists performing, lighting, recording, directing, hosting, publicity, choreography, audiences, props and production, framing the event as the meeting of several kinds of work.[S2]
A consolidated publicity draft instead says that the performers were settled only on 15 October, describes roughly half a month of rehearsal, and advertises 31 October at 19:30.[S3] Completing recruitment and settling the cast may refer to different steps; the wording may also reflect different accounts across drafts. Both formulations remain visible here. Neither is selected as an independently verified production date. The difference opens a precise question: how did recruitment, confirmation of participants and the start of rehearsal connect?
These dates are claims in historical publicity documents. File order cannot establish the order of the drafts, and advertised schedules do not replace attendance records or dated rehearsal logs.

## A second invitation: beyond the performance
Another publicity draft proposes a body-improvisation experience after the performance. Performers would lead audience members in bodily communication, renewed attention to the surrounding space and further stage creation.[S4] Read alongside the recruitment notice, it describes two forms of entry: joining the making of the work, then joining an activity after watching it.[S1][S4]
This is a documented proposal. It makes further questions concrete: how would the guidance begin, how would spectators enter the acting area, and how would the performance give way to participation? The documents and film stills below do not establish that the activity took place as proposed. A group visible in the stage film must not automatically be labelled as participating audience members.

## Three moments in one film: bodies and space
Open the 44:26 edited stage film, then use three verified stills to return to the moving image. All three were taken from the exact file uploaded for this public edition; their times belong only to this edition.[V1]
18:00: red light outlines a performer in a stride, with apparatus visible beside the legs. The image supports attention to the outline, stride and light. The apparatus does not establish a medical condition or a personal identity.[V3]
33:00: standing, crouching or sitting, and side-lying bodies occupy different levels in one acting area. This invites a question about how several positions compose the space. A still does not show how those positions developed; return to the film to examine what comes before and after.[V4]
38:00: extended arms in the foreground contrast with a lower group farther back, while different arm directions create another spatial comparison.[V5] Together, the three moments offer a practical viewing route: from one body and light, to the heights of several bodies, to depth and direction. This is an editorial reading sequence, not a claim about rehearsal stages, character identities or choreographic intentions.

## What the trailer, film and documents preserve
The 1:16 digital-edition trailer provides a promotional entry; the 44:26 edited film provides a longer view of the stage work. They remain separate editions, and trailer timestamps cannot be converted into film timestamps.[V2][V1] The film page also retains the existing main-channel edition. Without a verified timing map, each edition should be approached through its own entry point.
The documents preserve entry conditions, production accounts and proposed activities. Film stills preserve visible postures and space at specific moments in an edited record. The two kinds of evidence can support questions about the same project, but cannot substitute for one another. Whether open recruitment produced different working methods requires rehearsal evidence; a visible stage grouping does not establish agreement during production.

## Following the next evidence
Two checks now have concrete targets. First, compare the different descriptions of recruitment and cast confirmation with dated, revised rehearsal schedules. Second, compare the proposed post-performance improvisation with an independent record that can distinguish an invitation from an activity actually led.[S2][S3][S4]
The references below lead to each document, film and trailer. The sidebar connects the Cocoon project and its invitation-and-rehearsal dossier. This page establishes a traceable reading between public documents and visible images. Further public evidence can support a revised account of the process while this edition remains available.

两份面试记录的文件名分别带有2020年10月12日、13日的日期。这是定位线索，尚未由其他记录独立核实事件日期。经指定段落复核，可以补充招募阶段的普通创作任务：一份记录提示身体随音乐自然活动，不一定跳舞；双人即兴则把注意力转向对方的重量，以及远距离、无接触的呼应。[S5]
另一份记录提出纯肢体即兴与借助舞台道具的任务对照，并在不同段落继续提示：表达可以包括物件、行为或说话，不必一直使用舞蹈动作；另有为何选择复杂动作、能否考虑挥手等简单动作的追问。[S6] 这些提示来自不同段落，不能拼成同一人的连续试演，也不能据此认定两个任务均已完成。
从文稿保存的任务与反馈看，面试兼有试探共同工作方式的作用——这是本页的编辑解释。它让“无需专业基础”的招募条件获得一个更具体的对读入口：进入工作时，哪些表达方式被提出，双人如何建立关系？[S1][S5][S6] 尚无依据将这些提示直接对应到下方成片动作，或断言某项面试尝试进入最终编排。
记录A还提出十五日起至月底排练；既有公开文稿则回述十六日正式开始。[S5][S2] 前者是计划，后者是回述。两者差异的原因未知，不能直接改写为“延期一天”。公开来源页只提供上述普通任务的编辑摘述，原始面试稿、申请信息和私人经历保持不公开。

## 邀请并未止于入组：文稿还把观众带向演出之后
另一份宣传草稿提出正式演出后的身体即兴体验：由演员带领观众以身体沟通，重新感知周围空间，继续参与舞台创作。[S4] 与演员招募稿并读，可以看见两层进入方式：先招募参与制作的人，再邀请观看者参与演出后的活动。[S1][S4]
这是文稿层面明确的工作构想。它使我们能提出更具体的问题：带领怎样开始，观众如何进入演区，表演与体验的边界怎样交接？目前这几份文稿和下列成片静帧都不足以证明当晚按计划执行了这项活动，也不能把成片中的群体画面直接标作观众体验。

## 从同一成片的三个位置观察身体与空间
先打开44分26秒舞台作品剪辑版，再用三个已核静帧回到影片。它们取自该公开版的同一上传文件，时间只属于这一个版本。[V1]
18:00：红色光线勾勒出表演者的跨步姿态，腿部外侧可见装置。可观察的是身体轮廓、跨步与光的关系；装置本身不提供身体状况或人物身份的依据。[V3]
33:00：同一画面中出现站立、蹲坐和侧卧的身体，演区因此呈现不同高度。由此可以追问空间如何由多个位置共同构成。单帧没有保存位置形成的过程，应返回连续影片查看前后变化。[V4]
38:00：前景的伸臂与后景较低的人群形成前后层次，不同手臂方向提供另一种空间对照。[V5] 这三个观察点给观众一条可操作的观看路径：从一个身体与光的关系，转向多个身体的高度，再看前后景及方向。它是本次编辑安排的阅读顺序，不是对排练阶段、角色或编舞意图的断言。

## 预告、成片和文稿各自保留什么
1分16秒数字版预告承担宣传入口的作用；44分26秒剪辑版提供较长的舞台观看入口。两者分别保存，预告时码不能换算为成片时码。[V2][V1] 成片页还保留既有主频道版本，方便核对访问版本；没有经验证的跨版本时间对应时，应从各自入口阅读。
文稿记录进入条件、制作叙述和预期活动；成片静帧记录这一剪辑版本在特定时刻可见的姿态与空间。两种证据可以帮助提出同一个项目的问题，却不能彼此代替：开放招募是否带来了不同的工作方法，需要排练过程支持；舞台上可见的群体关系，也不能直接证明制作中的共识。

## 下一步怎样把线索变成过程叙述
最优先的两项核对已经具体化。第一，对照招募收束与演员确认的不同表述，寻找能标明日期和修订的排练安排。第二，对照演后身体即兴的计划，寻找独立记录来区分“提出活动”和“实际带领”。[S2][S3][S4]
下方来源可以逐条核对，观看引用可返回成片与预告，侧栏连接《茧房》项目和“邀请怎样进入排练”问题档案。这一页先让公开文稿与可见画面形成可追踪的阅读关系；后续获得新的公开证据时，再修订具体过程判断并保留本版。
saved_article_versions.body_en:
## Entering Cocoon through an invitation
The public materials for Cocoon offer several ways into the work. A recruitment notice invites people into rehearsal; publicity describes production as a period of shared commitment; a trailer introduces the work; and a 44:26 edited stage film makes bodies and stage space available for repeated viewing. Read together, they show how a production was invited, narrated and preserved. Establishing what happened at each step still requires process evidence.
The recruitment text seeks five to eight dancers, sets no age limit and does not require professional dance training. These are stated entry conditions, not evidence of the training of any person visible in the film.[S1] This reading follows the production timeline described in the documents, moves through three moments in one film edition, and returns to specific rehearsal questions.

## A production timeline with an unresolved difference
The text titled Sixteen Days and Nights of Anticipation at P4 presents a sequence: scheduling in September, recruitment completed in early October, rehearsals beginning on 16 October, and a public performance planned for 31 October. It lists performing, lighting, recording, directing, hosting, publicity, choreography, audiences, props and production, framing the event as the meeting of several kinds of work.[S2]
A consolidated publicity draft instead says that the performers were settled only on 15 October, describes roughly half a month of rehearsal, and advertises 31 October at 19:30.[S3] Completing recruitment and settling the cast may refer to different steps; the wording may also reflect different accounts across drafts. Both formulations remain visible here. Neither is selected as an independently verified production date. The difference opens a precise question: how did recruitment, confirmation of participants and the start of rehearsal connect?
These dates are claims in historical publicity documents. File order cannot establish the order of the drafts, and advertised schedules do not replace attendance records or dated rehearsal logs.

## How recruitment explored ways of working together
Two audition records carry 12 and 13 October 2020 in their filenames. These dates help locate the documents; they have not been independently established as event dates. Review of the specified paragraphs adds concrete task descriptions: one record prompts natural bodily responses to music without requiring dance. Paired improvisation directs attention toward another person's weight and toward responses across a distance without physical contact.[S5]
The other record proposes contrasting movement-only improvisation with tasks using stage objects. Prompts in separate paragraphs allow objects, actions or speech instead of continuous dance movement; another asks why complex movements were chosen and raises a simple gesture such as waving.[S6] These prompts must not be assembled into one person's continuous audition, nor do they establish that both tasks were completed.
The recorded tasks and feedback suggest that auditions also explored ways of working together. This is an editorial interpretation. It gives the recruitment condition of no required professional training a more concrete counterpart: what forms of expression were proposed, and how might a pair relate?[S1][S5][S6] There is no established link from these prompts to particular movements in the film below, or evidence that an audition experiment entered the final choreography.
Record A also proposes rehearsal from the fifteenth through the end of the month, while the existing public text recalls a formal start on the sixteenth.[S5][S2] One is a plan, the other a retrospective account. The reason for the difference is unknown; it cannot simply be described as a one-day postponement. The source pages publish editorial summaries of these ordinary tasks. Original audition documents, application information and personal experiences remain unpublished.

## A second invitation: beyond the performance
Another publicity draft proposes a body-improvisation experience after the performance. Performers would lead audience members in bodily communication, renewed attention to the surrounding space and further stage creation.[S4] Read alongside the recruitment notice, it describes two forms of entry: joining the making of the work, then joining an activity after watching it.[S1][S4]
This is a documented proposal. It makes further questions concrete: how would the guidance begin, how would spectators enter the acting area, and how would the performance give way to participation? The documents and film stills below do not establish that the activity took place as proposed. A group visible in the stage film must not automatically be labelled as participating audience members.

## Three moments in one film: bodies and space
Open the 44:26 edited stage film, then use three verified stills to return to the moving image. All three were taken from the exact file uploaded for this public edition; their times belong only to this edition.[V1]
18:00: red light outlines a performer in a stride, with apparatus visible beside the legs. The image supports attention to the outline, stride and light. The apparatus does not establish a medical condition or a personal identity.[V3]
33:00: standing, crouching or sitting, and side-lying bodies occupy different levels in one acting area. This invites a question about how several positions compose the space. A still does not show how those positions developed; return to the film to examine what comes before and after.[V4]
38:00: extended arms in the foreground contrast with a lower group farther back, while different arm directions create another spatial comparison.[V5] Together, the three moments offer a practical viewing route: from one body and light, to the heights of several bodies, to depth and direction. This is an editorial reading sequence, not a claim about rehearsal stages, character identities or choreographic intentions.

## What the trailer, film and documents preserve
The 1:16 digital-edition trailer provides a promotional entry; the 44:26 edited film provides a longer view of the stage work. They remain separate editions, and trailer timestamps cannot be converted into film timestamps.[V2][V1] The film page also retains the existing main-channel edition. Without a verified timing map, each edition should be approached through its own entry point.
The documents preserve entry conditions, production accounts and proposed activities. Film stills preserve visible postures and space at specific moments in an edited record. The two kinds of evidence can support questions about the same project, but cannot substitute for one another. Whether open recruitment produced different working methods requires rehearsal evidence; a visible stage grouping does not establish agreement during production.

## Following the next evidence
Two checks now have concrete targets. First, compare the different descriptions of recruitment and cast confirmation with dated, revised rehearsal schedules. Second, compare the proposed post-performance improvisation with an independent record that can distinguish an invitation from an activity actually led.[S2][S3][S4]
The references below lead to each document, film and trailer. The sidebar connects the Cocoon project and its invitation-and-rehearsal dossier. This page establishes a traceable reading between public documents and visible images. Further public evidence can support a revised account of the process while this edition remains available.

saved_article_versions.body:
《茧房》是2020年10月31日晚在北京P4剧场初次公演的舞蹈剧场，导演黄伊尹，编舞兼舞者郝杰。专业舞者与非专业参与者共同完成了这部关于偏见的作品。44分26秒剪辑版、演后报道和具名幕后谈，留下了具体的动作、观看角度与排练选择。[S7][S9]

## 三个动作反复展开，独舞停在筋疲力尽

> “其实我最后并没有走出那个圈，到最后是一个筋疲力尽的状态。”——陆洋[S12]

陆洋说，这段独舞从三个动作展开，是每次可能不同的即兴。他留到最后，反复做动作，想表现群体中不被理解、仍要朝自己方向走的那个人。独舞结束时，他给出的状态是耗尽力气，仍未走出自己的圈。[S12]

演后报道用“冲破茧房”概括主题；陆洋的自述却留下了突破没有完成的时刻。这两种叙述形成了张力：共同的方向是突破，个体的段落仍然可以停在受困之中。离开群体之后，一个人是否就能走出自己的限制？作品在这里保留了没有解决的问题。[S9][S12]

## 高跷段落为什么在意观众坐得高还是低

[P2]

郝杰谈高跷段落时，把一个具体的观看位置放进了创作：他用重复动作表达忏悔与救赎，却担心观众从二楼俯看，会觉得这个人渺小、理应如此。他希望观众从较低的角度面对这个身体。[S13]

> “我不想让人觉得这样的忏悔是渺小的”——郝杰[S13]

高跷段落的看点因此也包括观众与身体之间的高低关系。郝杰关心的不只是动作如何完成，还包括动作会被怎样理解。把这段自述与照片并看，可以注意他如何把“偏见”落实到一个空间选择上：观看位置也会参与判断的形成。[S13]

## 人离场了，灯光仍留给两只苹果

演后报道记下的结尾非常日常：郝杰和晓楠坐在舞台中央，各吃一只苹果；放下苹果后，两人相继离场，灯光让观众继续看向舞台。[S9]

[T2]：近景中的表演者把红苹果举到口部。

[T3]：两位表演者分坐左右，两只苹果放在中间。

[T4]：空舞台中央留下两只苹果，一束光仍照着它们。

再回到[T1]，一青一红、已经带着咬痕的苹果，早已作为近景出现在成片前部。这个剪辑安排把苹果放在了影像的前后两端。看完人的动作，再看仍留在光里的物件，可以注意观看对象怎样从身体转向它们留下的东西。[V1]

## 没有固定好的走位，让舞者重新学习怎样回应别人

当年的招募不要求专业舞蹈基础。演后报道则写到，非专业参与者的时间不容易协调；编舞郝杰从身体接触即兴开始带领排练，让参与者通过接触与互动产生动作。开放招募之后，团队仍需找到不同经验的人能够一起工作的方式。[S1][S9]

舞者何琳鹂记得，初期群舞走位还没有设计好。她每次都要用力记住自己该面对谁、该做什么动作。学校的训练会明确规定位置和动作角度，这里的工作方式使她起初疲惫，适应之后又感到新鲜。共同创作因此包含了具体的额外工作：一边寻找人与人的关系，一边记忆并组织演出。[S11]

同一篇访谈中，陈都把随音乐运动与用身体讲述故事区分开来。他谈到自己受过长期舞蹈训练，却仍希望补充身体表达的能力。这让“专业与非专业一起排练”多了一层含义：需要学习的并不只有第一次上台的人。[S11]

## 主题从一种歧视出发，在合作中扩大

黄伊尹在公开幕后谈中说，作品最初关注LGBTQ群体受到的歧视。在创作过程中，他与郝杰沟通，逐渐把范围扩大到更广泛的偏见：每个人都可能遭遇，也可能带着自己的判断看别人。[S10]

这条变化帮助理解前面的几种选择。陆洋谈的是脱离群体之后仍然存在的自我限制；郝杰把观看角度与判断联系起来；排练则要求不同背景的人在身体互动中寻找回应。它们从各自的位置进入“偏见”，留下的答案也并不相同。这是对几份公开自述的并读，不意味着作品最后解决了偏见。[S10][S11][S12][S13]

这次合作的时间很紧。10月29日的制作文章回述，9月敲定排期，10月16日开始排练，制作涉及近20人，月底面对观众。演后报道确认了10月31日晚的公演。近20人指制作规模，包括舞台之外的工作，并非演员人数。[S8][S9]

## 谁参与了这部作品

公开节目署名为：**导演黄伊尹；编舞兼舞者郝杰；舞者孙晓楠、陈都、谷雨岚、吴凡、何琳鹂、陆洋、陈润泽、史鹏涛。** P4剧场为出品方。[S7][S9]

何发的公开发言出现在参与和组织方式的讨论中：参与者可以提出意见，也可以来讨论自己未来想做的剧场项目。这段发言提供了P4如何邀请后续创作的线索；作品导演署名仍归黄伊尹。[S10]

## 继续观看与查阅

可以先看44分26秒舞台剪辑版，也可以从[T2]进入结尾，再回看[T1]。[V1] 想了解动作由何而来，就读陆洋和郝杰的自述；想了解排练怎样开展，就读何琳鹂和陈都的回顾。[S12][S13][S11]

1分16秒数字版预告是独立的宣传版本。[V2] 招募、面试任务与演后身体即兴的计划保留在下方来源中，可以继续追问舞台之前和之后怎样组织参与。[S1][S4][S5][S6]
saved_article_versions.body_en:
Cocoon is a dance-theatre work first performed on the evening of 31 October 2020 at P4 Theater in Beijing, directed by Huang Yiyin, with choreography and performance by Hao Jie. Professionally trained dancers and nonprofessional participants made this work about prejudice together. A 44:26 edited film, a post-performance report and named backstage accounts preserve its movements, viewing positions and rehearsal choices.[S7][S9]

## Three movements unfold, and the solo ends in exhaustion

> “In fact, I never left that circle in the end; by the end I was exhausted.” — Lu Yang, translated from Chinese[S12]

Lu Yang describes a solo improvised from three movements, potentially different each time. He stays until the end, repeating movements to portray someone within a group who remains misunderstood but wants to follow their own direction. The ending he describes is exhaustion, still within his own circle.[S12]

The post-performance report describes the theme as breaking out of the cocoon; Lu Yang's account preserves a moment in which that breakthrough remains incomplete. There is tension between these two accounts: a shared direction towards breaking through can coexist with an individual's continued confinement. Does leaving a group mean escaping one's own limits? The work leaves that question unresolved here.[S9][S12]

## Why the stilt passage cares whether the audience sits higher or lower

[P2]

Discussing the stilt passage, Hao Jie makes the audience's position part of the work. He uses repeated movement to express repentance and redemption, but worries that viewers looking down from the second floor might see the person as small and deserving of that position. He wants viewers to encounter the body from a lower angle.[S13]

> “I don't want people to feel that this repentance is insignificant.” — Hao Jie, translated from Chinese[S13]

The height relationship between spectator and performer is therefore part of what to look at. Hao Jie is concerned both with performing the movement and with how it will be understood. Reading his account alongside the photograph brings a spatial choice into focus: where a spectator looks from can take part in forming a judgement.[S13]

## The people leave; the light stays with two apples

The post-performance report describes an ordinary action at the ending: Hao Jie and Xiaonan sit at centre stage, each eating an apple. After putting the apples down, they leave one after the other; the lighting directs the audience to keep looking at the stage.[S9]

[T2]: in close-up, a performer holds a red apple to their mouth.

[T3]: two performers sit on opposite sides, with two apples between them.

[T4]: two apples remain at the centre of an empty stage, still under a beam of light.

Return to [T1]: a green apple and a red apple, already bearing bite marks, appear in close-up near the beginning of the film. The edit places the apples near both ends of the screen work. After watching the bodies, look at the objects remaining in the light: attention can shift from the performers to what they leave behind.[V1]

## Unsettled positions ask dancers to learn how to respond to others

The recruitment notice did not require professional dance training. The post-performance report describes difficulties coordinating nonprofessional participants' schedules. Choreographer Hao Jie began with contact improvisation, generating movement through physical contact and interaction. After opening recruitment, the team still had to find ways for people with different experience to work together.[S1][S9]

Dancer He Linli recalls that the group choreography's positions had not been settled at the outset. Each time, she had to concentrate on remembering whom to face and which movement to make. School training specified positions and angles precisely; this different way of working initially tired her, then felt fresh as she adapted. Making the work together required additional, concrete labour: finding relationships while remembering and organising a performance.[S11]

In the same interview, Chen Du distinguishes moving to music from telling a story through the body. Despite years of dance training, he wanted to develop his capacity for bodily expression. This gives rehearsals involving professionals and nonprofessionals another dimension: learning was not confined to people stepping onstage for the first time.[S11]

## A theme begins with one form of discrimination and broadens through collaboration

In the published backstage conversation, Huang Yiyin says the work began with discrimination against LGBTQ people. Through conversations with Hao Jie during creation, its scope broadened towards prejudice more generally: something people may encounter and also bring to their own judgements of others.[S10]

This development helps connect the choices described above. Lu Yang discusses limits that remain after separating from a group; Hao Jie links viewing position with judgement; rehearsals ask people with different backgrounds to find responses through bodily interaction. They approach prejudice from different positions and do not arrive at identical answers. This is a reading across published accounts, not a claim that the work ultimately resolves prejudice.[S10][S11][S12][S13]

The collaboration had little time. A production article published on 29 October recalls scheduling in September, rehearsals beginning on 16 October and a production involving almost twenty people, working towards an audience at the month's end. The later report confirms the performance on the evening of 31 October. Almost twenty refers to the production team, including work offstage, not the number of performers.[S8][S9]

## Who made the work

The published programme credits **director Huang Yiyin; choreographer and dancer Hao Jie; and dancers Sun Xiaonan, Chen Du, Gu Yulan, Wu Fan, He Linli, Lu Yang, Chen Runze and Shi Pengtao.** P4 Theater is credited as producer.[S7][S9]

He Fa's published remarks concern participation and organisation: participants can offer opinions and discuss theatre projects they might want to make in future. His account gives a lead into how P4 invited further work; the directing credit for Cocoon remains Huang Yiyin's.[S10]

## Continue watching and reading

Start with the 44:26 edited stage film, or enter the ending at [T2] and return to [T1].[V1] Read Lu Yang and Hao Jie on the choices behind the movements; read He Linli and Chen Du on how rehearsals unfolded.[S12][S13][S11]

The 1:16 digital-edition trailer is a separate promotional version.[V2] The recruitment notice, audition task summaries and proposed post-performance improvisation remain in the sources below, offering further leads into participation before and after the stage work.[S1][S4][S5][S6]

saved_article_versions.body:
## 从一个招募问题进入《茧房》
《茧房》的公开材料留下了几种不同的相遇方式：招募文案邀请人走进排练，宣传稿把制作叙述成一段共同投入的时间，预告邀请观众接近作品，44分26秒剪辑版则让舞台上的身体和空间可以反复观看。把它们放在一起，首先能读到的是一次创作怎样被邀请、讲述和保存；从邀请到实际排练的每一步，仍需相应过程记录。
招募稿提出招收5至8名舞者，年龄不限，也不要求专业舞蹈基础。这是公开写出的进入条件，不能由此推断成片中谁具有或不具有专业训练。[S1] 下面的阅读沿着文稿中的制作时间，进入同一成片的三个观察点，再回到尚待核实的排练问题。

## 文稿给出时间线，也留下一个需要对照的差异
《在p4剧场的16个日与夜的期盼》把制作写成连续的推进：9月敲定排期，10月初完成招募，10月16日开始排练，面向10月31日公演。它还列举演员、舞者、灯光、记录、导演、主持、宣传、编导、观众、道具和制作等环节，显示这篇宣传文字如何把演出呈现为多种工作的汇合。[S2]
另一份整合宣传草稿却写演员在10月15日才定下来，排练时间约半个月，并列出10月31日19:30的演出安排。[S3] “完成招募”和“演员定下来”可能指不同环节，也可能来自不同稿本的叙述。这里保留两种措辞，不选一个日期冒充已经核实的排练史。这是可以继续追查的具体线索：招募收束、人员确认和开始排练之间，究竟怎样衔接？
这些日期目前是历史宣传文稿中的说法。文件保存顺序不足以确定稿本先后，宣传中的时间安排也不能替代出勤表或逐日排练记录。

## 邀请并未止于入组：文稿还把观众带向演出之后
另一份宣传草稿提出正式演出后的身体即兴体验：由演员带领观众以身体沟通，重新感知周围空间，继续参与舞台创作。[S4] 与演员招募稿并读，可以看见两层进入方式：先招募参与制作的人，再邀请观看者参与演出后的活动。[S1][S4]
这是文稿层面明确的工作构想。它使我们能提出更具体的问题：带领怎样开始，观众如何进入演区，表演与体验的边界怎样交接？目前这几份文稿和下列成片静帧都不足以证明当晚按计划执行了这项活动，也不能把成片中的群体画面直接标作观众体验。

## 从同一成片的三个位置观察身体与空间
先打开44分26秒舞台作品剪辑版，再用三个已核静帧回到影片。它们取自该公开版的同一上传文件，时间只属于这一个版本。[V1]
18:00：红色光线勾勒出表演者的跨步姿态，腿部外侧可见装置。可观察的是身体轮廓、跨步与光的关系；装置本身不提供身体状况或人物身份的依据。[V3]
33:00：同一画面中出现站立、蹲坐和侧卧的身体，演区因此呈现不同高度。由此可以追问空间如何由多个位置共同构成。单帧没有保存位置形成的过程，应返回连续影片查看前后变化。[V4]
38:00：前景的伸臂与后景较低的人群形成前后层次，不同手臂方向提供另一种空间对照。[V5] 这三个观察点给观众一条可操作的观看路径：从一个身体与光的关系，转向多个身体的高度，再看前后景及方向。它是本次编辑安排的阅读顺序，不是对排练阶段、角色或编舞意图的断言。

## 预告、成片和文稿各自保留什么
1分16秒数字版预告承担宣传入口的作用；44分26秒剪辑版提供较长的舞台观看入口。两者分别保存，预告时码不能换算为成片时码。[V2][V1] 成片页还保留既有主频道版本，方便核对访问版本；没有经验证的跨版本时间对应时，应从各自入口阅读。
文稿记录进入条件、制作叙述和预期活动；成片静帧记录这一剪辑版本在特定时刻可见的姿态与空间。两种证据可以帮助提出同一个项目的问题，却不能彼此代替：开放招募是否带来了不同的工作方法，需要排练过程支持；舞台上可见的群体关系，也不能直接证明制作中的共识。

## 下一步怎样把线索变成过程叙述
最优先的两项核对已经具体化。第一，对照招募收束与演员确认的不同表述，寻找能标明日期和修订的排练安排。第二，对照演后身体即兴的计划，寻找独立记录来区分“提出活动”和“实际带领”。[S2][S3][S4]
下方来源可以逐条核对，观看引用可返回成片与预告，侧栏连接《茧房》项目和“邀请怎样进入排练”问题档案。这一页先让公开文稿与可见画面形成可追踪的阅读关系；后续获得新的公开证据时，再修订具体过程判断并保留本版。
saved_article_versions.body_en:
## Entering Cocoon through an invitation
The public materials for Cocoon offer several ways into the work. A recruitment notice invites people into rehearsal; publicity describes production as a period of shared commitment; a trailer introduces the work; and a 44:26 edited stage film makes bodies and stage space available for repeated viewing. Read together, they show how a production was invited, narrated and preserved. Establishing what happened at each step still requires process evidence.
The recruitment text seeks five to eight dancers, sets no age limit and does not require professional dance training. These are stated entry conditions, not evidence of the training of any person visible in the film.[S1] This reading follows the production timeline described in the documents, moves through three moments in one film edition, and returns to specific rehearsal questions.

## A production timeline with an unresolved difference
The text titled Sixteen Days and Nights of Anticipation at P4 presents a sequence: scheduling in September, recruitment completed in early October, rehearsals beginning on 16 October, and a public performance planned for 31 October. It lists performing, lighting, recording, directing, hosting, publicity, choreography, audiences, props and production, framing the event as the meeting of several kinds of work.[S2]
A consolidated publicity draft instead says that the performers were settled only on 15 October, describes roughly half a month of rehearsal, and advertises 31 October at 19:30.[S3] Completing recruitment and settling the cast may refer to different steps; the wording may also reflect different accounts across drafts. Both formulations remain visible here. Neither is selected as an independently verified production date. The difference opens a precise question: how did recruitment, confirmation of participants and the start of rehearsal connect?
These dates are claims in historical publicity documents. File order cannot establish the order of the drafts, and advertised schedules do not replace attendance records or dated rehearsal logs.

## A second invitation: beyond the performance
Another publicity draft proposes a body-improvisation experience after the performance. Performers would lead audience members in bodily communication, renewed attention to the surrounding space and further stage creation.[S4] Read alongside the recruitment notice, it describes two forms of entry: joining the making of the work, then joining an activity after watching it.[S1][S4]
This is a documented proposal. It makes further questions concrete: how would the guidance begin, how would spectators enter the acting area, and how would the performance give way to participation? The documents and film stills below do not establish that the activity took place as proposed. A group visible in the stage film must not automatically be labelled as participating audience members.

## Three moments in one film: bodies and space
Open the 44:26 edited stage film, then use three verified stills to return to the moving image. All three were taken from the exact file uploaded for this public edition; their times belong only to this edition.[V1]
18:00: red light outlines a performer in a stride, with apparatus visible beside the legs. The image supports attention to the outline, stride and light. The apparatus does not establish a medical condition or a personal identity.[V3]
33:00: standing, crouching or sitting, and side-lying bodies occupy different levels in one acting area. This invites a question about how several positions compose the space. A still does not show how those positions developed; return to the film to examine what comes before and after.[V4]
38:00: extended arms in the foreground contrast with a lower group farther back, while different arm directions create another spatial comparison.[V5] Together, the three moments offer a practical viewing route: from one body and light, to the heights of several bodies, to depth and direction. This is an editorial reading sequence, not a claim about rehearsal stages, character identities or choreographic intentions.

## What the trailer, film and documents preserve
The 1:16 digital-edition trailer provides a promotional entry; the 44:26 edited film provides a longer view of the stage work. They remain separate editions, and trailer timestamps cannot be converted into film timestamps.[V2][V1] The film page also retains the existing main-channel edition. Without a verified timing map, each edition should be approached through its own entry point.
The documents preserve entry conditions, production accounts and proposed activities. Film stills preserve visible postures and space at specific moments in an edited record. The two kinds of evidence can support questions about the same project, but cannot substitute for one another. Whether open recruitment produced different working methods requires rehearsal evidence; a visible stage grouping does not establish agreement during production.

## Following the next evidence
Two checks now have concrete targets. First, compare the different descriptions of recruitment and cast confirmation with dated, revised rehearsal schedules. Second, compare the proposed post-performance improvisation with an independent record that can distinguish an invitation from an activity actually led.[S2][S3][S4]
The references below lead to each document, film and trailer. The sidebar connects the Cocoon project and its invitation-and-rehearsal dossier. This page establishes a traceable reading between public documents and visible images. Further public evidence can support a revised account of the process while this edition remains available.

saved_article_versions.body:
## 从一个招募问题进入《茧房》
《茧房》的公开材料留下了几种不同的相遇方式：招募文案邀请人走进排练，宣传稿把制作叙述成一段共同投入的时间，预告邀请观众接近作品，44分26秒剪辑版则让舞台上的身体和空间可以反复观看。把它们放在一起，首先能读到的是一次创作怎样被邀请、讲述和保存；从邀请到实际排练的每一步，仍需相应过程记录。
招募稿提出招收5至8名舞者，年龄不限，也不要求专业舞蹈基础。这是公开写出的进入条件，不能由此推断成片中谁具有或不具有专业训练。[S1] 下面的阅读沿着文稿中的制作时间，进入同一成片的三个观察点，再回到尚待核实的排练问题。

## 文稿给出时间线，也留下一个需要对照的差异
《在p4剧场的16个日与夜的期盼》把制作写成连续的推进：9月敲定排期，10月初完成招募，10月16日开始排练，面向10月31日公演。它还列举演员、舞者、灯光、记录、导演、主持、宣传、编导、观众、道具和制作等环节，显示这篇宣传文字如何把演出呈现为多种工作的汇合。[S2]
另一份整合宣传草稿却写演员在10月15日才定下来，排练时间约半个月，并列出10月31日19:30的演出安排。[S3] “完成招募”和“演员定下来”可能指不同环节，也可能来自不同稿本的叙述。这里保留两种措辞，不选一个日期冒充已经核实的排练史。这是可以继续追查的具体线索：招募收束、人员确认和开始排练之间，究竟怎样衔接？
这些日期目前是历史宣传文稿中的说法。文件保存顺序不足以确定稿本先后，宣传中的时间安排也不能替代出勤表或逐日排练记录。

## 招募阶段怎样试探共同工作
两份面试记录的文件名分别带有2020年10月12日、13日的日期。这是定位线索，尚未由其他记录独立核实事件日期。经指定段落复核，可以补充招募阶段的普通创作任务：一份记录提示身体随音乐自然活动，不一定跳舞；双人即兴则把注意力转向对方的重量，以及远距离、无接触的呼应。[S5]
另一份记录提出纯肢体即兴与借助舞台道具的任务对照，并在不同段落继续提示：表达可以包括物件、行为或说话，不必一直使用舞蹈动作；另有为何选择复杂动作、能否考虑挥手等简单动作的追问。[S6] 这些提示来自不同段落，不能拼成同一人的连续试演，也不能据此认定两个任务均已完成。
从文稿保存的任务与反馈看，面试兼有试探共同工作方式的作用——这是本页的编辑解释。它让“无需专业基础”的招募条件获得一个更具体的对读入口：进入工作时，哪些表达方式被提出，双人如何建立关系？[S1][S5][S6] 尚无依据将这些提示直接对应到下方成片动作，或断言某项面试尝试进入最终编排。
记录A还提出十五日起至月底排练；既有公开文稿则回述十六日正式开始。[S5][S2] 前者是计划，后者是回述。两者差异的原因未知，不能直接改写为“延期一天”。公开来源页只提供上述普通任务的编辑摘述，原始面试稿、申请信息和私人经历保持不公开。

## 邀请并未止于入组：文稿还把观众带向演出之后
另一份宣传草稿提出正式演出后的身体即兴体验：由演员带领观众以身体沟通，重新感知周围空间，继续参与舞台创作。[S4] 与演员招募稿并读，可以看见两层进入方式：先招募参与制作的人，再邀请观看者参与演出后的活动。[S1][S4]
这是文稿层面明确的工作构想。它使我们能提出更具体的问题：带领怎样开始，观众如何进入演区，表演与体验的边界怎样交接？目前这几份文稿和下列成片静帧都不足以证明当晚按计划执行了这项活动，也不能把成片中的群体画面直接标作观众体验。

## 从同一成片的三个位置观察身体与空间
先打开44分26秒舞台作品剪辑版，再用三个已核静帧回到影片。它们取自该公开版的同一上传文件，时间只属于这一个版本。[V1]
18:00：红色光线勾勒出表演者的跨步姿态，腿部外侧可见装置。可观察的是身体轮廓、跨步与光的关系；装置本身不提供身体状况或人物身份的依据。[V3]
33:00：同一画面中出现站立、蹲坐和侧卧的身体，演区因此呈现不同高度。由此可以追问空间如何由多个位置共同构成。单帧没有保存位置形成的过程，应返回连续影片查看前后变化。[V4]
38:00：前景的伸臂与后景较低的人群形成前后层次，不同手臂方向提供另一种空间对照。[V5] 这三个观察点给观众一条可操作的观看路径：从一个身体与光的关系，转向多个身体的高度，再看前后景及方向。它是本次编辑安排的阅读顺序，不是对排练阶段、角色或编舞意图的断言。

## 预告、成片和文稿各自保留什么
1分16秒数字版预告承担宣传入口的作用；44分26秒剪辑版提供较长的舞台观看入口。两者分别保存，预告时码不能换算为成片时码。[V2][V1] 成片页还保留既有主频道版本，方便核对访问版本；没有经验证的跨版本时间对应时，应从各自入口阅读。
文稿记录进入条件、制作叙述和预期活动；成片静帧记录这一剪辑版本在特定时刻可见的姿态与空间。两种证据可以帮助提出同一个项目的问题，却不能彼此代替：开放招募是否带来了不同的工作方法，需要排练过程支持；舞台上可见的群体关系，也不能直接证明制作中的共识。

## 下一步怎样把线索变成过程叙述
最优先的两项核对已经具体化。第一，对照招募收束与演员确认的不同表述，寻找能标明日期和修订的排练安排。第二，对照演后身体即兴的计划，寻找独立记录来区分“提出活动”和“实际带领”。[S2][S3][S4]
下方来源可以逐条核对，观看引用可返回成片与预告，侧栏连接《茧房》项目和“邀请怎样进入排练”问题档案。这一页先让公开文稿与可见画面形成可追踪的阅读关系；后续获得新的公开证据时，再修订具体过程判断并保留本版。
saved_article_versions.body_en:
## Entering Cocoon through an invitation
The public materials for Cocoon offer several ways into the work. A recruitment notice invites people into rehearsal; publicity describes production as a period of shared commitment; a trailer introduces the work; and a 44:26 edited stage film makes bodies and stage space available for repeated viewing. Read together, they show how a production was invited, narrated and preserved. Establishing what happened at each step still requires process evidence.
The recruitment text seeks five to eight dancers, sets no age limit and does not require professional dance training. These are stated entry conditions, not evidence of the training of any person visible in the film.[S1] This reading follows the production timeline described in the documents, moves through three moments in one film edition, and returns to specific rehearsal questions.

## A production timeline with an unresolved difference
The text titled Sixteen Days and Nights of Anticipation at P4 presents a sequence: scheduling in September, recruitment completed in early October, rehearsals beginning on 16 October, and a public performance planned for 31 October. It lists performing, lighting, recording, directing, hosting, publicity, choreography, audiences, props and production, framing the event as the meeting of several kinds of work.[S2]
A consolidated publicity draft instead says that the performers were settled only on 15 October, describes roughly half a month of rehearsal, and advertises 31 October at 19:30.[S3] Completing recruitment and settling the cast may refer to different steps; the wording may also reflect different accounts across drafts. Both formulations remain visible here. Neither is selected as an independently verified production date. The difference opens a precise question: how did recruitment, confirmation of participants and the start of rehearsal connect?
These dates are claims in historical publicity documents. File order cannot establish the order of the drafts, and advertised schedules do not replace attendance records or dated rehearsal logs.

## How recruitment explored ways of working together
Two audition records carry 12 and 13 October 2020 in their filenames. These dates help locate the documents; they have not been independently established as event dates. Review of the specified paragraphs adds concrete task descriptions: one record prompts natural bodily responses to music without requiring dance. Paired improvisation directs attention toward another person's weight and toward responses across a distance without physical contact.[S5]
The other record proposes contrasting movement-only improvisation with tasks using stage objects. Prompts in separate paragraphs allow objects, actions or speech instead of continuous dance movement; another asks why complex movements were chosen and raises a simple gesture such as waving.[S6] These prompts must not be assembled into one person's continuous audition, nor do they establish that both tasks were completed.
The recorded tasks and feedback suggest that auditions also explored ways of working together. This is an editorial interpretation. It gives the recruitment condition of no required professional training a more concrete counterpart: what forms of expression were proposed, and how might a pair relate?[S1][S5][S6] There is no established link from these prompts to particular movements in the film below, or evidence that an audition experiment entered the final choreography.
Record A also proposes rehearsal from the fifteenth through the end of the month, while the existing public text recalls a formal start on the sixteenth.[S5][S2] One is a plan, the other a retrospective account. The reason for the difference is unknown; it cannot simply be described as a one-day postponement. The source pages publish editorial summaries of these ordinary tasks. Original audition documents, application information and personal experiences remain unpublished.

## A second invitation: beyond the performance
Another publicity draft proposes a body-improvisation experience after the performance. Performers would lead audience members in bodily communication, renewed attention to the surrounding space and further stage creation.[S4] Read alongside the recruitment notice, it describes two forms of entry: joining the making of the work, then joining an activity after watching it.[S1][S4]
This is a documented proposal. It makes further questions concrete: how would the guidance begin, how would spectators enter the acting area, and how would the performance give way to participation? The documents and film stills below do not establish that the activity took place as proposed. A group visible in the stage film must not automatically be labelled as participating audience members.

## Three moments in one film: bodies and space
Open the 44:26 edited stage film, then use three verified stills to return to the moving image. All three were taken from the exact file uploaded for this public edition; their times belong only to this edition.[V1]
18:00: red light outlines a performer in a stride, with apparatus visible beside the legs. The image supports attention to the outline, stride and light. The apparatus does not establish a medical condition or a personal identity.[V3]
33:00: standing, crouching or sitting, and side-lying bodies occupy different levels in one acting area. This invites a question about how several positions compose the space. A still does not show how those positions developed; return to the film to examine what comes before and after.[V4]
38:00: extended arms in the foreground contrast with a lower group farther back, while different arm directions create another spatial comparison.[V5] Together, the three moments offer a practical viewing route: from one body and light, to the heights of several bodies, to depth and direction. This is an editorial reading sequence, not a claim about rehearsal stages, character identities or choreographic intentions.

## What the trailer, film and documents preserve
The 1:16 digital-edition trailer provides a promotional entry; the 44:26 edited film provides a longer view of the stage work. They remain separate editions, and trailer timestamps cannot be converted into film timestamps.[V2][V1] The film page also retains the existing main-channel edition. Without a verified timing map, each edition should be approached through its own entry point.
The documents preserve entry conditions, production accounts and proposed activities. Film stills preserve visible postures and space at specific moments in an edited record. The two kinds of evidence can support questions about the same project, but cannot substitute for one another. Whether open recruitment produced different working methods requires rehearsal evidence; a visible stage grouping does not establish agreement during production.

## Following the next evidence
Two checks now have concrete targets. First, compare the different descriptions of recruitment and cast confirmation with dated, revised rehearsal schedules. Second, compare the proposed post-performance improvisation with an independent record that can distinguish an invitation from an activity actually led.[S2][S3][S4]
The references below lead to each document, film and trailer. The sidebar connects the Cocoon project and its invitation-and-rehearsal dossier. This page establishes a traceable reading between public documents and visible images. Further public evidence can support a revised account of the process while this edition remains available.

saved_article_versions.body:
《茧房》是2020年10月31日晚在北京P4剧场初次公演的舞蹈剧场，导演黄伊尹，编舞兼舞者郝杰。专业舞者与非专业参与者共同完成了这部关于偏见的作品。44分26秒剪辑版、演后报道和具名幕后谈，留下了具体的动作、观看角度与排练选择。[S7][S9]

## 三个动作反复展开，独舞停在筋疲力尽

> “其实我最后并没有走出那个圈，到最后是一个筋疲力尽的状态。”——陆洋[S12]

陆洋说，这段独舞从三个动作展开，是每次可能不同的即兴。他留到最后，反复做动作，想表现群体中不被理解、仍要朝自己方向走的那个人。独舞结束时，他给出的状态是耗尽力气，仍未走出自己的圈。[S12]

演后报道用“冲破茧房”概括主题；陆洋的自述却留下了突破没有完成的时刻。这两种叙述形成了张力：共同的方向是突破，个体的段落仍然可以停在受困之中。离开群体之后，一个人是否就能走出自己的限制？作品在这里保留了没有解决的问题。[S9][S12]

## 高跷段落为什么在意观众坐得高还是低

[P2]

郝杰谈高跷段落时，把一个具体的观看位置放进了创作：他用重复动作表达忏悔与救赎，却担心观众从二楼俯看，会觉得这个人渺小、理应如此。他希望观众从较低的角度面对这个身体。[S13]

> “我不想让人觉得这样的忏悔是渺小的”——郝杰[S13]

高跷段落的看点因此也包括观众与身体之间的高低关系。郝杰关心的不只是动作如何完成，还包括动作会被怎样理解。把这段自述与照片并看，可以注意他如何把“偏见”落实到一个空间选择上：观看位置也会参与判断的形成。[S13]

## 人离场了，灯光仍留给两只苹果

演后报道记下的结尾非常日常：郝杰和晓楠坐在舞台中央，各吃一只苹果；放下苹果后，两人相继离场，灯光让观众继续看向舞台。[S9]

[T2]：近景中的表演者把红苹果举到口部。

[T3]：两位表演者分坐左右，两只苹果放在中间。

[T4]：空舞台中央留下两只苹果，一束光仍照着它们。

再回到[T1]，一青一红、已经带着咬痕的苹果，早已作为近景出现在成片前部。这个剪辑安排把苹果放在了影像的前后两端。看完人的动作，再看仍留在光里的物件，可以注意观看对象怎样从身体转向它们留下的东西。[V1]

## 没有固定好的走位，让舞者重新学习怎样回应别人

当年的招募不要求专业舞蹈基础。演后报道则写到，非专业参与者的时间不容易协调；编舞郝杰从身体接触即兴开始带领排练，让参与者通过接触与互动产生动作。开放招募之后，团队仍需找到不同经验的人能够一起工作的方式。[S1][S9]

舞者何琳鹂记得，初期群舞走位还没有设计好。她每次都要用力记住自己该面对谁、该做什么动作。学校的训练会明确规定位置和动作角度，这里的工作方式使她起初疲惫，适应之后又感到新鲜。共同创作因此包含了具体的额外工作：一边寻找人与人的关系，一边记忆并组织演出。[S11]

同一篇访谈中，陈都把随音乐运动与用身体讲述故事区分开来。他谈到自己受过长期舞蹈训练，却仍希望补充身体表达的能力。这让“专业与非专业一起排练”多了一层含义：需要学习的并不只有第一次上台的人。[S11]

## 主题从一种歧视出发，在合作中扩大

黄伊尹在公开幕后谈中说，作品最初关注LGBTQ群体受到的歧视。在创作过程中，他与郝杰沟通，逐渐把范围扩大到更广泛的偏见：每个人都可能遭遇，也可能带着自己的判断看别人。[S10]

这条变化帮助理解前面的几种选择。陆洋谈的是脱离群体之后仍然存在的自我限制；郝杰把观看角度与判断联系起来；排练则要求不同背景的人在身体互动中寻找回应。它们从各自的位置进入“偏见”，留下的答案也并不相同。这是对几份公开自述的并读，不意味着作品最后解决了偏见。[S10][S11][S12][S13]

这次合作的时间很紧。10月29日的制作文章回述，9月敲定排期，10月16日开始排练，制作涉及近20人，月底面对观众。演后报道确认了10月31日晚的公演。近20人指制作规模，包括舞台之外的工作，并非演员人数。[S8][S9]

## 谁参与了这部作品

公开节目署名为：**导演黄伊尹；编舞兼舞者郝杰；舞者孙晓楠、陈都、谷雨岚、吴凡、何琳鹂、陆洋、陈润泽、史鹏涛。** P4剧场为出品方。[S7][S9]

何发的公开发言出现在参与和组织方式的讨论中：参与者可以提出意见，也可以来讨论自己未来想做的剧场项目。这段发言提供了P4如何邀请后续创作的线索；作品导演署名仍归黄伊尹。[S10]

## 继续观看与查阅

可以先看44分26秒舞台剪辑版，也可以从[T2]进入结尾，再回看[T1]。[V1] 想了解动作由何而来，就读陆洋和郝杰的自述；想了解排练怎样开展，就读何琳鹂和陈都的回顾。[S12][S13][S11]

1分16秒数字版预告是独立的宣传版本。[V2] 招募、面试任务与演后身体即兴的计划保留在下方来源中，可以继续追问舞台之前和之后怎样组织参与。[S1][S4][S5][S6]
saved_article_versions.body_en:
Cocoon is a dance-theatre work first performed on the evening of 31 October 2020 at P4 Theater in Beijing, directed by Huang Yiyin, with choreography and performance by Hao Jie. Professionally trained dancers and nonprofessional participants made this work about prejudice together. A 44:26 edited film, a post-performance report and named backstage accounts preserve its movements, viewing positions and rehearsal choices.[S7][S9]

## Three movements unfold, and the solo ends in exhaustion

> “In fact, I never left that circle in the end; by the end I was exhausted.” — Lu Yang, translated from Chinese[S12]

Lu Yang describes a solo improvised from three movements, potentially different each time. He stays until the end, repeating movements to portray someone within a group who remains misunderstood but wants to follow their own direction. The ending he describes is exhaustion, still within his own circle.[S12]

The post-performance report describes the theme as breaking out of the cocoon; Lu Yang's account preserves a moment in which that breakthrough remains incomplete. There is tension between these two accounts: a shared direction towards breaking through can coexist with an individual's continued confinement. Does leaving a group mean escaping one's own limits? The work leaves that question unresolved here.[S9][S12]

## Why the stilt passage cares whether the audience sits higher or lower

[P2]

Discussing the stilt passage, Hao Jie makes the audience's position part of the work. He uses repeated movement to express repentance and redemption, but worries that viewers looking down from the second floor might see the person as small and deserving of that position. He wants viewers to encounter the body from a lower angle.[S13]

> “I don't want people to feel that this repentance is insignificant.” — Hao Jie, translated from Chinese[S13]

The height relationship between spectator and performer is therefore part of what to look at. Hao Jie is concerned both with performing the movement and with how it will be understood. Reading his account alongside the photograph brings a spatial choice into focus: where a spectator looks from can take part in forming a judgement.[S13]

## The people leave; the light stays with two apples

The post-performance report describes an ordinary action at the ending: Hao Jie and Xiaonan sit at centre stage, each eating an apple. After putting the apples down, they leave one after the other; the lighting directs the audience to keep looking at the stage.[S9]

[T2]: in close-up, a performer holds a red apple to their mouth.

[T3]: two performers sit on opposite sides, with two apples between them.

[T4]: two apples remain at the centre of an empty stage, still under a beam of light.

Return to [T1]: a green apple and a red apple, already bearing bite marks, appear in close-up near the beginning of the film. The edit places the apples near both ends of the screen work. After watching the bodies, look at the objects remaining in the light: attention can shift from the performers to what they leave behind.[V1]

## Unsettled positions ask dancers to learn how to respond to others

The recruitment notice did not require professional dance training. The post-performance report describes difficulties coordinating nonprofessional participants' schedules. Choreographer Hao Jie began with contact improvisation, generating movement through physical contact and interaction. After opening recruitment, the team still had to find ways for people with different experience to work together.[S1][S9]

Dancer He Linli recalls that the group choreography's positions had not been settled at the outset. Each time, she had to concentrate on remembering whom to face and which movement to make. School training specified positions and angles precisely; this different way of working initially tired her, then felt fresh as she adapted. Making the work together required additional, concrete labour: finding relationships while remembering and organising a performance.[S11]

In the same interview, Chen Du distinguishes moving to music from telling a story through the body. Despite years of dance training, he wanted to develop his capacity for bodily expression. This gives rehearsals involving professionals and nonprofessionals another dimension: learning was not confined to people stepping onstage for the first time.[S11]

## A theme begins with one form of discrimination and broadens through collaboration

In the published backstage conversation, Huang Yiyin says the work began with discrimination against LGBTQ people. Through conversations with Hao Jie during creation, its scope broadened towards prejudice more generally: something people may encounter and also bring to their own judgements of others.[S10]

This development helps connect the choices described above. Lu Yang discusses limits that remain after separating from a group; Hao Jie links viewing position with judgement; rehearsals ask people with different backgrounds to find responses through bodily interaction. They approach prejudice from different positions and do not arrive at identical answers. This is a reading across published accounts, not a claim that the work ultimately resolves prejudice.[S10][S11][S12][S13]

The collaboration had little time. A production article published on 29 October recalls scheduling in September, rehearsals beginning on 16 October and a production involving almost twenty people, working towards an audience at the month's end. The later report confirms the performance on the evening of 31 October. Almost twenty refers to the production team, including work offstage, not the number of performers.[S8][S9]

## Who made the work

The published programme credits **director Huang Yiyin; choreographer and dancer Hao Jie; and dancers Sun Xiaonan, Chen Du, Gu Yulan, Wu Fan, He Linli, Lu Yang, Chen Runze and Shi Pengtao.** P4 Theater is credited as producer.[S7][S9]

He Fa's published remarks concern participation and organisation: participants can offer opinions and discuss theatre projects they might want to make in future. His account gives a lead into how P4 invited further work; the directing credit for Cocoon remains Huang Yiyin's.[S10]

## Continue watching and reading

Start with the 44:26 edited stage film, or enter the ending at [T2] and return to [T1].[V1] Read Lu Yang and Hao Jie on the choices behind the movements; read He Linli and Chen Du on how rehearsals unfolded.[S12][S13][S11]

The 1:16 digital-edition trailer is a separate promotional version.[V2] The recruitment notice, audition task summaries and proposed post-performance improvisation remain in the sources below, offering further leads into participation before and after the stage work.[S1][S4][S5][S6]

presentation.notes_en: Meanings of the solo and stilt passage come from the creators’ published accounts. The circle is not translated into a claim about real-life experiences, and the work’s LGBTQ subject does not establish any participant’s sexual orientation. The apple sequence is reported by the performance article; the four time points describe stills. Names follow published text, not facial identification. Original “Photos for” labels are not photographer credits. The complete source file matches the approved upload receipt by SHA-256; times belong only to this 44:26 edit and player seek precision depends on the platform. Exact boundaries of the solo and stilt passage and the second-floor seating arrangement are not established. This update did not involve continuous listening or viewing.
presentation.notes_zh: 独舞和高跷的含义来自创作者公开自述；“圈”不转换为现实遭遇，作品的LGBTQ议题不用于推断参与者性取向。苹果动作经过来自演后报道，四个时间点对应静帧观察；人物姓名沿用原文，不由面孔辨认。原始照片标签Photos for不作摄影署名。成片完整源文件与既有上传回执SHA-256一致，时间只适用于这支44:26剪辑版；播放器定位精度以平台为准。尚未登记独舞、高跷段落精确起止，未确认二楼座位安排；本轮没有连续听看影片。

saved_article_versions.revisionNote_en: Rewritten for viewers using the published programme and four named backstage conversations, following the solo, stilts, apples, rehearsal positions and thematic development. Adds two photographs checked against the original publication chain and apple timings verified against the uploaded film. Preserves both earlier editions and their sources.
saved_article_versions.summary: 陆洋留下未完成的突破，郝杰希望改变观看高跷的角度，结尾把目光留给两只苹果。沿五组材料走进这部舞蹈剧场。
saved_article_versions.summary_en: Lu Yang leaves a breakthrough unfinished; Hao Jie seeks a different angle on the stilt passage; the ending holds our gaze on two apples. Enter the work through five groups of materials.

# 幸福王国：从一笔教育资金，问到一碗牛肉面

## 给出教育的理由，追问仍未结束
想获得一笔钱，若是为了改善教育，是否就不再是贪婪？《幸福王国》Unit E的前段谈话让这个理由接受连续追问。回应者提出资金的用途，问题又回到“想要更多”本身：一个用途，能否改变人们对欲望的判断？给出理由，并没有让这场戏剧中的问答就此结束。[V1]

这支约9分26秒的公开章节保存了一段问答；公开发布说明将它关联到2023年7月22日北京望京的活动。黑帘、红绿灯光、席地交流的人，构成了彼此距离很近的空间。这里的“审判屎家庭”是活动设定的戏剧情境，不是现实司法程序，也不是本馆对任何人的现实指控。[S1][V1]

## 俯身持棒：言语怎样进入身体
中段的一处画面里，一位参与者在红光中俯身，手握棒状物，棒端朝向地面；另一些人坐在近旁。[V1]

把这个姿势与前面的问答放在一起看，可以留意言语判断怎样转为身体行动，以及旁观者与行动者如何共处一个狭小空间。姿势、发问与在场观看，在这里成为可以连着阅读的线索。

## 从教育道路，问到面馆怎样经营
后段提出另一种生活选择：开牛肉面馆。讨论随后落到牛肉、熬汤、能否赚钱和经营成本。一个有关教育道路的判断，变成了可以逐项追问的生计方案：提出另一条路之后，还要说明这条路怎样运作。[V1]

牛肉面馆的转折使这段谈话变得具体。回应者不仅需要提出选择，还需要面对实际细节。一个选择如何从设想走向可以讨论的实际安排，成为这一转折留下的问题。

## 这场活动怎样邀请参与
7月19日发表的招募，先列出一个人呼吸、感知、移动的能力，再把“仍不满足”写进戏剧指控。公告邀请参与者来审判，并手工制作可以消灭这一戏剧对象的生物。它预告7月22日19:00在北京望京举行，免费，限8人；这些是参与规则与计划，不能当作现场人数或全部任务已经完成的证据。[S1]

Unit E记录了其中一段问答，而非整场活动。谁在提问、谁在回应、谁采取动作，是本章可以继续观察的位置；没有可靠的身份对应，就不把片中人绑定到具体姓名或固定职务。招募中的手工任务是否完成，本章不能回答。[V1]

## 从这个章节继续观看
三个场面连起来，保存的是判断被提出、理由被回应、回应又受到检验的过程。观看时可以跟随问题如何变化：从资金用途，到身体动作，再到一碗面需要哪些现实条件。[V1]

公开发布说明记载，章节开始前约4分14秒没有记录，且片头、片尾的对话都已在进行。因此不能把本章推作另一段“一分钟思考”指令的直接结果，也不能从片尾推断整场最终判决。整片入口保留这段问答的观看顺序；场面边界尚未核定，本页不提供精确时间跳转。[V1]

# Happiness Kingdom: from education funding to a bowl of beef noodles

## A reason for education does not end the questioning
If someone wants money to improve education, does that make the desire less greedy? Early in Happiness Kingdom, Unit E, that justification meets further questions. A respondent explains what the money would be used for; the discussion returns to wanting more. Can a proposed use change the judgement of a desire? Giving a reason does not bring this theatrical exchange to a close.[V1]

This public chapter, approximately 9 minutes 26 seconds long, preserves an exchange that its public release description associates with an activity in Wangjing, Beijing, on 22 July 2023. Black curtains, red and green lighting, and people conversing on the floor form a space of close proximity. The Trial of the Shit Family is the activity's theatrical premise, not a real judicial proceeding or an accusation made by this library against anyone.[S1][V1]

## Bending forward with a rod: from speech to bodily action
In one image from the middle passage, a participant bends forward in red light, holding a rod-like object with its end directed towards the floor. Others sit nearby.[V1]

Read alongside the earlier questions, the posture invites attention to how verbal judgement becomes bodily action, and how those watching share a small space with the person acting. Posture, questioning and watching together offer connected ways of reading this passage.

## From an educational path to running a noodle shop
Later, another choice is proposed: opening a beef-noodle shop. The discussion turns to beef, making broth, whether the business can make money, and operating costs. A judgement about education becomes a livelihood proposal that can be questioned detail by detail. Once another path is suggested, how would it actually work?[V1]

The noodle-shop turn makes the exchange concrete. The respondent must address practical details as well as state a choice. The turn leaves a practical question: how does a proposed choice become an arrangement whose details can be discussed?

## How the activity invited participation
Published on 19 July, the recruitment notice lists a person's capacities to breathe, sense and move, then makes continued dissatisfaction part of its theatrical accusation. It invites participants to conduct a trial and make a creature by hand that could eliminate the theatrical object of that trial. The notice announces 19:00 on 22 July in Wangjing, Beijing, free admission and a limit of eight people. These are participation rules and plans, not proof of actual attendance or completion of every task.[S1]

Unit E preserves one exchange within the activity, not the whole event. Who asks, who responds and who acts are positions a viewer can observe here. Without reliable identity evidence, the people on screen are not assigned names or fixed duties. This chapter cannot establish whether the announced making task was completed.[V1]

## Continuing through the chapter
Together, these scenes preserve a process in which judgements are proposed, reasons are offered, and those responses meet further scrutiny. Follow how the questions change: from a use for money, to bodily action, to the practical conditions behind a bowl of noodles.[V1]

The public release description reports about 4 minutes 14 seconds of unrecorded event time before this chapter, with dialogue already underway at both ends. The chapter therefore cannot be treated as the direct outcome of a one-minute thinking instruction in another segment, nor can its ending establish a final verdict for the event. The full-chapter link preserves the order of this exchange. Scene boundaries remain unverified, so this page supplies no exact-time links.[V1]
